newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips soar in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips soar in active trade.

text.p: Nigerian equities closed higher on Wednesday, buoyed by blue chip gains, traders said.
They said blue chip stocks rose on strong demand, pushing the all-share index further to 7840.59 from Tuesday's 7772.49.
Food and beverages shares saw generous gains.
Nestle, the food giant, closed at 62.50 naira, up 1.25 naira, while Coca-Cola bottler Nigerian Bottling Company finished 1.10 naira higher at 45.30 naira.
Conglomerates also advanced on renewed interest in PZ PZIN.LG which added nine kobo to 23.20 naira and CFAO which rose six kobo to 2.70 naira.
But Lever Brothers was the biggest beneficiary in the group, rising to 21.00 naira with a 30 kobo appreciation, followed by UAC which climbed by 20 kobo to 11.30 naira.
Surging bank shares continued to impress market analysts. They said the nation's big banks ended stronger as investors sought to consolidate their holding.
Afribank was 6.25 naira, up 25 kobo, same as First Bank which closed at 14.75 naira. UBA rose 30 kobo to 10.80 naira and Union Bank added 20 kobo to finish at 12.70 naira.
Total ended 60 kobo higher at 71.00 naira, hot on the trail of fellow oil products marketer Unipetrol, which at 73.50 naira gained 40 kobo on Wednesday.
Furniture maker Vono Products rose by the maximum five percent allowed when it chalked up 13 kobo to 2.80 naira as a dealer crossed some 1.6 million units.

Niger Insurance shot up to 4.35 naira, adding 10 kobo, Royal Insurance rose five kobo to 3.55 naira while Alumaco, Industrial Gases IGAS and Nigerian Enamelware Company each finished 10 kobo better at 3.20 naira, 14.75 naira and 5.80 naira, respectively.
Smithkline Beecham was still in a free fall as surplus shares remained in the market. It fell 30 kobo to 6.65 naira despite one dealer's attempt to mop up more than 100,000 units.

Stationery company WTN dropped 10 kobo to 6.80 naira and National Salt Company lost nine kobo at 6.20 naira while publishing firm Daily Times saw its price lowered by one kobo to 50 kobo due to lack of any interest, dealers said.
